files.content:
# Todo Application Requirements Analysis Report

## 1. Business Overview

### 1.1 Purpose
The Todo Application is a privacy-focused task management system that allows individual users to create, organize, and track their personal tasks in a secure environment. Each user's data is completely isolated from other users, ensuring complete privacy for all todo items.

### 1.2 Key Features
- User account management with registration, login, and profile customization
- Comprehensive todo creation with title, description, and optional date tracking
- Full edit history tracking for all todo modifications
- Soft delete functionality with trash management
- Advanced filtering and sorting capabilities
- Strict data privacy with no cross-user data access

### 1.3 Business Value
This application addresses the need for individuals to have a private, secure, and feature-rich task management solution. In an era where data privacy is increasingly important, the application provides users with complete control over their personal task data while offering robust functionality to enhance productivity.

## 2. Functional Requirements

### 2.1 User Account Management

#### 2.1.1 User Registration
WHEN a guest accesses the application, THE system SHALL provide a registration form with email and password fields.

WHEN a user submits valid registration information, THE system SHALL create a new user account and send a verification email.

IF a user attempts to register with an email that already exists, THEN THE system SHALL display an error message indicating the email is already in use.

#### 2.1.2 User Login
WHEN a user provides valid email and password credentials, THE system SHALL authenticate the user and establish a session.

IF a user provides invalid credentials, THEN THE system SHALL display an appropriate error message and log the failed attempt.

#### 2.1.3 Password Management
WHEN an authenticated user requests to change their password, THE system SHALL require the current password and a new password.

WHEN an authenticated user submits a valid password change request, THE system SHALL update the user's password and invalidate all existing sessions except the current one.

#### 2.1.4 Account Deletion
WHEN an authenticated user requests to delete their account, THE system SHALL prompt for confirmation of this irreversible action.

WHEN an authenticated user confirms account deletion, THE system SHALL permanently remove all user data including todos, profile information, and edit history.

### 2.2 User Profile Management

#### 2.2.1 Profile Creation
WHEN a user successfully registers, THE system SHALL create a default profile with the user's email as the display name.

#### 2.2.2 Profile Modification
WHEN an authenticated user updates their display name, THE system SHALL save the new display name and confirm the update.

THE system SHALL prevent users from viewing profiles of other users.

### 2.3 Todo Creation and Management

#### 2.3.1 Todo Creation
WHEN an authenticated user creates a new todo with a title, THE system SHALL save the todo with the following attributes:
- Title (required)
- Description (optional)
- Start date (optional)
- Due date (optional)
- Creation date (automatically set)
- Completion status (automatically set to incomplete)

IF a user attempts to create a todo without a title, THEN THE system SHALL reject the creation request and indicate that the title is required.

#### 2.3.2 Todo Viewing
WHEN an authenticated user accesses their todo list, THE system SHALL display only their own todos with pagination.

WHEN an authenticated user views their todo list, THE system SHALL display for each todo:
- Title
- Completion status
- Start date (if set)
- Due date (if set)
- Creation date

WHEN an authenticated user selects a specific todo, THE system SHALL display all todo details including full description.

#### 2.3.3 Todo Completion Status
WHEN an authenticated user marks a todo as complete, THE system SHALL update the completion status and record the completion date.

WHEN an authenticated user marks a completed todo as incomplete, THE system SHALL update the completion status and clear the completion date.

#### 2.3.4 Todo Editing
WHEN an authenticated user modifies any attribute of their todo (title, description, start date, or due date), THE system SHALL save the changes and create a new entry in the todo's edit history.

### 2.4 Edit History Tracking

#### 2.4.1 History Creation
WHEN an authenticated user edits any attribute of their todo, THE system SHALL create a new history entry containing:
- Timestamp of the edit
- Previous and new values for each modified field (title, description, start date, due date)

#### 2.4.2 History Viewing
WHEN an authenticated user accesses the edit history for their todo, THE system SHALL display all history entries sorted from most recent to oldest.

### 2.5 Todo Deletion and Trash Management

#### 2.5.1 Soft Deletion
WHEN an authenticated user deletes their todo, THE system SHALL mark the todo as deleted without removing it from the database.

WHEN an authenticated user views their regular todo list, THE system SHALL not display deleted todos.

#### 2.5.2 Trash Management
WHEN an authenticated user accesses the trash view, THE system SHALL display all their deleted todos with pagination.

WHEN an authenticated user restores a todo from trash, THE system SHALL remove the deleted status and return the todo to the regular todo list.

WHEN an authenticated user permanently deletes a todo from trash, THE system SHALL remove the todo and all associated edit history from the database.

### 2.6 Filtering and Sorting

#### 2.6.1 Todo Filtering
WHEN an authenticated user applies a completion status filter, THE system SHALL display only todos matching the selected filter:
- All todos (complete and incomplete)
- Only complete todos
- Only incomplete todos

#### 2.6.2 Todo Sorting
WHEN an authenticated user sorts their todo list by creation date, THE system SHALL order todos with newest first or oldest first based on user selection.

WHEN an authenticated user sorts their todo list by start date, THE system SHALL order todos with earliest first or latest first based on user selection, placing todos without start dates at the end.

WHEN an authenticated user sorts their todo list by due date, THE system SHALL order todos with earliest first or latest first based on user selection, placing todos without due dates at the end.

## 3. Non-Functional Requirements

### 3.1 Privacy and Security

THE system SHALL ensure that each user can only access their own todos, profile, and edit history.

THE system SHALL not provide any mechanism for users to access, view, or share another user's data.

THE system SHALL encrypt user passwords using industry-standard hashing algorithms.

### 3.2 Data Integrity

THE system SHALL maintain a complete history of all todo modifications for as long as the todo exists.

THE system SHALL permanently remove all user data upon account deletion.

### 3.3 Performance

WHEN a user accesses their todo list, THE system SHALL load and display the first page of results within 2 seconds.

WHEN a user performs a filtering or sorting operation, THE system SHALL update the todo list within 1 second.

### 3.4 Data Retention

THE system SHALL retain user todos and associated edit history for the duration of the user's account.

WHEN a user permanently deletes a todo, THE system SHALL remove all associated data immediately.

WHEN a user deletes their account, THE system SHALL remove all user data within 24 hours.

## 4. User Workflows

### 4.1 User Registration and Login Workflow

```mermaid
graph LR
  A["Access Application"] --> B["View Registration/Login Options"]
  B --> C["Select Registration"]
  C --> D["Fill Registration Form"]
  D --> E["Submit Registration"]
  E --> F{"Registration Valid?"}
  F -->|"Yes"| G["Create Account"]
  F -->|"No"| H["Show Error Messages"]
  G --> I["Send Verification Email"]
  H --> D
  I --> J["Show Success Message"]
  B --> K["Select Login"]
  K --> L["Fill Login Form"]
  L --> M["Submit Credentials"]
  M --> N{"Credentials Valid?"}
  N -->|"Yes"| O["Grant Access"]
  N -->|"No"| P["Show Error Message"]
  P --> L
```

### 4.2 Todo Creation and Management Workflow

```mermaid
graph LR
  A["Access Todo List"] --> B["View Existing Todos"]
  B --> C["Create New Todo"]
  C --> D["Fill Todo Details"]
  D --> E["Save Todo"]
  E --> F{"Todo Valid?"}
  F -->|"Yes"| G["Add to Todo List"]
  F -->|"No"| H["Show Validation Errors"]
  H --> D
  B --> I["Select Todo"]
  I --> J["View Todo Details"]
  J --> K["Edit Todo"]
  K --> L["Modify Todo Fields"]
  L --> M["Save Changes"]
  M --> N["Update Todo and History"]
  J --> O["Toggle Completion"]
  O --> P["Update Status"]
  J --> Q["Delete Todo"]
  Q --> R["Mark as Deleted"]
```

### 4.3 Trash Management Workflow

```mermaid
graph LR
  A["Access Trash"] --> B["View Deleted Todos"]
  B --> C["Restore Todo"]
  C --> D["Remove Deleted Status"]
  D --> E["Return to Todo List"]
  B --> F["Permanently Delete"]
  F --> G["Confirm Deletion"]
  G --> H{"Confirmed?"}
  H -->|"Yes"| I["Remove from Database"]
  H -->|"No"| B
```

## 5. Business Rules

### 5.1 User Account Rules

THE system SHALL require a unique email address for each user account.

THE system SHALL enforce strong password requirements during registration and password changes.

THE system SHALL automatically log out users after a period of inactivity.

### 5.2 Todo Management Rules

THE system SHALL set all newly created todos to an incomplete status by default.

THE system SHALL preserve all todo edit history for the lifetime of the the todo.

THE system SHALL only allow users to manage todos they created.

### 5.3 Data Privacy Rules

THE system SHALL not expose any user data to other users under any circumstances.

THE system SHALL not include user data in any analytics or reporting features without explicit consent.

THE system SHALL implement role-based access controls to ensure users can only access their own data.

## 6. Error Handling

### 6.1 Authentication Errors

IF a user attempts to register with invalid information, THEN THE system SHALL display specific error messages for each invalid field.

IF a user attempts to log in with invalid credentials, THEN THE system SHALL display a generic error message without specifying which part was incorrect.

### 6.2 Todo Management Errors

IF a user attempts to create a todo without a title, THEN THE system SHALL prevent creation and highlight the required field.

IF a user attempts to access a todo they do not own, THEN THE system SHALL return a not found error.

IF the system encounters an internal error while processing a todo operation, THEN THE system SHALL log the error and display a user-friendly message.

## 7. Success Metrics

THE system SHALL be considered successful if it meets the following criteria:
- User account creation success rate exceeds 99%
- Todo operations complete within specified time limits 95% of the time
- No security breaches occur during the first year of operation
- User satisfaction ratings exceed 4.5/5.0 in post-registration surveys
- System uptime exceeds 99.5% monthly

## 8. Testing Scenarios

### 8.1 Account Management Scenarios

1. User successfully registers with valid information
2. User fails to register with duplicate email
3. User successfully logs in with valid credentials
4. User fails to log in with invalid credentials
5. User successfully changes password
6. User successfully deletes account and all associated data

### 8.2 Todo Management Scenarios

1. User creates todo with all fields populated
2. User creates todo with only required fields
3. User views todo list with pagination
4. User filters todos by completion status
5. User sorts todos by different criteria
6. User edits todo and verifies history is recorded
7. User toggles todo completion status
8. User deletes todo and verifies it moves to trash

### 8.3 Trash Management Scenarios

1. User views trash and sees deleted todos
2. User restores todo from trash
3. User permanently deletes todo from trash
4. User verifies permanent deletion removes all associated data

### 8.4 Privacy Scenarios

1. User cannot access another user's todos
2. User cannot view another user's profile
3. Deleted user data is completely removed from system

## 9. Acceptance Criteria

### 9.1 Functional Acceptance Criteria

- Users can register, login, and manage their accounts
- Users can create, view, edit, and delete todos
- All todo operations are logged in edit history
- Filtering and sorting work according to specifications
- Trash functionality enables restore and permanent deletion
- Data privacy is strictly enforced between users

### 9.2 Performance Acceptance Criteria

- Page load times meet specified requirements
- Filtering and sorting operations complete within time limits
- System handles concurrent users without degradation

### 9.3 Security Acceptance Criteria

- User data isolation is verified through testing
- Password encryption meets security standards
- Account deletion completely removes all user data

## 10. Future Considerations

WHERE the application gains significant user adoption, THE system SHALL support:
- Category or tagging systems for todos
- Recurring todo functionality
- Collaboration features with invited users
- Data export capabilities
- Mobile application integration

instruction:
# Multi-User Todo Application

## User Account

- Users sign up with email and password
- Users log in with email and password
- Users can change their password
- Users can delete their account (all their todos, including those in trash, are permanently deleted)

## User Profile

- Each user has a profile with: display name
- Users can edit their display name
- Users cannot view other users' profiles (this is a private todo app)

## Creating Todos

- Users can create a todo with:
  - Title (required)
  - Description (optional, can be left empty)
  - Start date (optional, can be left empty)
  - Due date (optional, can be left empty)
- Newly created todos are incomplete by default

## Viewing Todos

- Users can view a list of their own todos
- The list is paginated
- Each todo in the list shows: title, completion status, start date (if set), due date (if set), and creation date
- Users can view a single todo to see all its details including full description

## Completing Todos

- Users can mark a todo as complete
- Users can mark a todo as incomplete
- This is a simple toggle between two states

## Editing Todos

- Users can edit their todo's title, description, start date, and due date
- Every edit is recorded in the todo's history

## Edit History

- Each todo has an edit history
- Every time a todo is edited, a history entry is created
- Each history entry records:
  - When the edit was made
  - What the title was changed to (if changed)
  - What the description was changed to (if changed)
  - What the start date was changed to (if changed)
  - What the due date was changed to (if changed)
- Users can view the full edit history of any of their todos
- History entries are sorted from most recent to oldest

## Deleting Todos

- Users can delete their own todos
- Deleted todos are not permanently removed (soft delete)
- Deleted todos no longer appear in the normal todo list

## Trash

- Users can view a list of their deleted todos (trash)
- The trash list is paginated
- Users can restore a deleted todo from the trash (it returns to the normal todo list)
- Users can permanently delete a todo from the trash
- Permanently deleting a todo also deletes its edit history

## Filtering Todos

- Users can filter their todo list by completion status:
  - All todos
  - Only complete todos
  - Only incomplete todos

## Sorting Todos

- Users can sort their todo list by:
  - Creation date (newest first or oldest first)
  - Start date (earliest first or latest first)
  - Due date (earliest first or latest first)
- Todos without a start date appear at the end when sorting by start date
- Todos without a due date appear at the end when sorting by due date

## Privacy

- Each user's todos are completely private
- Users can only see their own todos
- There is no way to view, access, or share another user's todos

models.description:
todo app actors table.

This table stores core information about users who can authenticate and use the todo application. It contains credential information for authentication as well as profile data that is visible to the user. All todos and related data in the system belong to a specific user from this table.

The table implements email-based authentication with password hashing for security. Each user has a unique email address that serves as their login identifier. Profile information includes a display name that can be updated by the user.

Users in this table can create, view, edit, and delete their own todos. They have full control over their data including the ability to permanently delete their account, which removes all associated todos, history, and other personal data from the system.
models.name: todo_app_todo_users

plainFields.description: User's email address used for authentication and communication. Must be unique across all users in the system.
plainFields.name: email

plainFields.description: Hashed password for user authentication. Uses bcrypt hashing for security.
plainFields.name: password

plainFields.description: User's display name that appears in the application interface. Can be updated by the user as needed.
plainFields.name: display_name

plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was initially created.
plainFields.name: created_at

plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was last updated.
plainFields.name: updated_at

models.description:
JWT session tokens for user authentication with access and refresh token support for todo users.

This table manages authentication sessions for todo app users, storing both access and refresh tokens
with their expiration times. It maintains client connection metadata and tracks session usage for
security auditing. Each session is tied to a specific user and supports token refresh workflows.

The table implements secure session management with automatic expiration and last usage tracking.
It enforces uniqueness constraints on both access and refresh tokens to prevent conflicts. Sessions
are linked to users through the todo_app_todo_user_id foreign key with a one-to-many relationship,
enabling users to have multiple concurrent sessions.
models.name: todo_app_todo_user_sessions

plainFields.description: Access token for authentication
plainFields.name: access_token

plainFields.description: Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens
plainFields.name: refresh_token

plainFields.description: IP address of the client when the session was created
plainFields.name: ip

plainFields.description: User agent string of the client when the session was created
plainFields.name: user_agent

plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created
plainFields.name: created_at

plainFields.description: Timestamp when the access token expires
plainFields.name: access_token_expires_at

plainFields.description: Timestamp when the refresh token expires
plainFields.name: refresh_token_expires_at

plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was last used
plainFields.name: last_used_at

models.description:
Password reset tokens with expiration for secure user password recovery workflow in the todo application.

This table manages the password reset process for todo users, storing unique tokens that are emailed to users when they request a password reset. Each token has an expiration time after which it becomes invalid. The table links to the main user account for verification during the reset process.

The tokens are designed to be single-use - once a password reset is completed using a token, that token is removed from this table. Expired tokens are also regularly cleaned up to maintain table performance.

When users successfully reset their password, the related entries in this table are automatically deleted as part of the password reset completion process.

foreignFields.description: Reference to the todo user who requested the password reset. Links to the main user account that the reset token is valid for. {@link todo_app_todo_users.id}
foreignFields.name: todo_user_id

models.name: todo_app_todo_user_password_resets

plainFields.description: Cryptographically secure random token string sent to the user's email address. Used to authenticate the password reset request. Should be sufficiently long and random to prevent guessing attacks.
plainFields.name: reset_token

plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset token expires. After this time, the token becomes invalid and cannot be used for password reset. Typically set to a short duration (e.g., 1 hour) from creation time.
plainFields.name: expires_at

plainFields.description: When this password reset record was created. Used for tracking token age and debugging purposes.
plainFields.name: created_at

models.description:
Email verification tokens for user registration confirmation in the todo application.

This table stores email verification tokens generated when a new user registers. Each token is associated with a specific user and has an expiration time. Once a user clicks the verification link containing this token, their email is confirmed and they can fully access the application. The token is then invalidated.

Tokens are automatically cleaned up after expiration to maintain database performance. The system ensures tokens are cryptographically secure and single-use to prevent security vulnerabilities.

foreignFields.description: The todo user associated with this email verification token. {@link todo_app_todo_users.id}
foreignFields.name: todo_app_todo_user_id

models.name: todo_app_todo_user_email_verifications

plainFields.description: Cryptographically secure token value used for email verification. This is a unique, random string that is emailed to the user as part of a verification link.
plainFields.name: code

plainFields.description: Expiration timestamp for the email verification token. After this time, the token becomes invalid and the user must request a new verification email.
plainFields.name: expired_at

plainFields.description: Timestamp when the email verification token was created.
plainFields.name: created_at

models.description:
Application configuration settings that control global behavior and feature flags for the todo application. 

This table stores system-wide configuration values that can be used to enable or disable features, 
set application limits, define operational parameters, and control other global behaviors. 
The configuration uses a key-value structure where each key represents a specific setting 
and the value contains the configuration data in JSON format.

Configurations are identified by unique keys and can be scoped to specific namespaces 
for better organization. The system maintains version history for configuration changes 
and includes temporal fields for audit trails.
models.name: todo_app_configurations

plainFields.description: Unique key identifying the configuration setting. Must follow naming conventions with lowercase letters, numbers, and underscores only. Examples: 'feature_enable_edit_history', 'limit_max_todos_per_user', 'auth_password_min_length'.
plainFields.name: key

plainFields.description: Namespace for organizing configurations. Allows grouping related settings together. Examples: 'auth', 'todo', 'system', 'limits'.
plainFields.name: namespace

plainFields.description: JSON-formatted configuration value. Can store simple values like strings and numbers, or complex objects and arrays as needed for the specific configuration setting.
plainFields.name: value

plainFields.name: description

plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration entry was created. Used for audit trails and tracking when settings were introduced.
plainFields.name: created_at

plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration entry was last updated. Used for audit trails and tracking when settings were modified.
plainFields.name: updated_at

plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration entry was deleted (soft delete). Allows configuration entries to be archived without permanent removal.
plainFields.name: deleted_at

models.description:
todo_app_system_settings

This table stores key-value pairs of system configuration settings, including feature flags, operational parameters, and behavioral configurations that control the overall application functionality. Each setting is uniquely identified by its name and contains serialized value data along with descriptive metadata.

Settings are versioned through the todo_app_system_setting_histories table to maintain an audit trail of all changes.

Use this table to store configuration parameters that affect the entire application, such as:
- Feature enablement flags
- Performance tuning parameters
- Integration endpoint configurations
- Business rule thresholds
- Operational mode settings
models.name: todo_app_system_settings

plainFields.name: value

plainFields.description: Human-readable description explaining the purpose and usage of this system setting.

models.description:
Tracking table for database schema versions and migration history in the todo application.

This table maintains a chronological record of all schema changes applied to the application database. Each entry represents a specific version of the database schema, allowing for reliable migration management and rollback capabilities when needed.

The version tracking system ensures that database changes are applied consistently across different environments (development, staging, production) and provides audit trails for schema evolution. It supports automated migration workflows by recording which migrations have been applied and when.

Each version entry includes metadata about the migration such as version identifier, description, and timestamps for when the migration was applied. The system prevents duplicate migrations by enforcing unique version identifiers.
models.name: todo_app_schema_versions

plainFields.description: Primary human-readable identifier for this schema version. Typically follows semantic versioning patterns (e.g., v1.0.0) or migration naming conventions (e.g., 20241201153000_initial_setup).
plainFields.name: version

plainFields.description: Brief description of what changes this schema version introduces. Explains the purpose and impact of the migration for operational understanding.
plainFields.name: description

plainFields.description: Timestamp when this schema version was applied to the database. Used for migration ordering and audit trail purposes.
plainFields.name: applied_at

models.name: todo_app_todos
models.description:
Main todo items created by users in the todo application, containing all core metadata including title, description, and temporal fields for task management.

This table represents the primary business entity for the todo application where users store their task items. Each todo is owned by a specific user who is authenticated through the todo_app_todo_users relationship.

Key aspects of this table include:

- Complete ownership tracking through foreign key relationships to user accounts
- Soft deletion support for the trash system
- Full temporal tracking with created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at timestamps
- Status tracking with completed boolean field
- Proper indexing strategy for common query patterns

The table is designed to support all user operations including:

- Viewing personal todo lists with pagination
- Creating new todos with optional metadata
- Updating todos with full edit history tracking (handled by History component)
- Soft deleting todos which moves them to trash (handled by Trash component)

### `todo_app_todo_users`

todo app actors table.

This table stores core information about users who can authenticate and
use the todo application. It contains credential information for
authentication as well as profile data that is visible to the user. All
todos and related data in the system belong to a specific user from this
table.

The table implements email-based authentication with password hashing for
security. Each user has a unique email address that serves as their login
identifier. Profile information includes a display name that can be
updated by the user.

Users in this table can create, view, edit, and delete their own todos.
They have full control over their data including the ability to
permanently delete their account, which removes all associated todos,
history, and other personal data from the system.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`
  > User's email address used for authentication and communication. Must be
  > unique across all users in the system.
- `password`: Hashed password for user authentication. Uses bcrypt hashing for security.
- `display_name`
  > User's display name that appears in the application interface. Can be
  > updated by the user as needed.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the user account was initially created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the user account was last updated.

### `todo_app_todo_user_sessions`

JWT session tokens for user authentication with access and refresh token
support for todo users.

This table manages authentication sessions for todo app users, storing
both access and refresh tokens
with their expiration times. It maintains client connection metadata and
tracks session usage for
security auditing. Each session is tied to a specific user and supports
token refresh workflows.

The table implements secure session management with automatic expiration
and last usage tracking.
It enforces uniqueness constraints on both access and refresh tokens to
prevent conflicts. Sessions
are linked to users through the todo_app_todo_user_id foreign key with a
one-to-many relationship,
enabling users to have multiple concurrent sessions.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key
- `todo_app_todo_user_id`: todo_app_todo_users.id
- `access_token`: Access token for authentication
- `refresh_token`: Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens
- `ip`: IP address of the client when the session was created
- `user_agent`: User agent string of the client when the session was created
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the session was created
- `access_token_expires_at`: Timestamp when the access token expires
- `refresh_token_expires_at`: Timestamp when the refresh token expires
- `last_used_at`: Timestamp when the session was last used

### `todo_app_todo_user_password_resets`

Password reset tokens with expiration for secure user password recovery
workflow in the todo application.

This table manages the password reset process for todo users, storing
unique tokens that are emailed to users when they request a password
reset. Each token has an expiration time after which it becomes invalid.
The table links to the main user account for verification during the
reset process.

The tokens are designed to be single-use - once a password reset is
completed using a token, that token is removed from this table. Expired
tokens are also regularly cleaned up to maintain table performance.

When users successfully reset their password, the related entries in this
table are automatically deleted as part of the password reset completion
process.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_user_id`
  > Reference to the todo user who requested the password reset. Links to the
  > main user account that the reset token is valid for. {@link
  > todo_app_todo_users.id}
- `reset_token`
  > Cryptographically secure random token string sent to the user's email
  > address. Used to authenticate the password reset request. Should be
  > sufficiently long and random to prevent guessing attacks.
- `expires_at`
  > Timestamp when the password reset token expires. After this time, the
  > token becomes invalid and cannot be used for password reset. Typically
  > set to a short duration (e.g., 1 hour) from creation time.
- `created_at`
  > When this password reset record was created. Used for tracking token age
  > and debugging purposes.

### `todo_app_todo_user_email_verifications`

Email verification tokens for user registration confirmation in the todo
application.

This table stores email verification tokens generated when a new user
registers. Each token is associated with a specific user and has an
expiration time. Once a user clicks the verification link containing this
token, their email is confirmed and they can fully access the
application. The token is then invalidated.

Tokens are automatically cleaned up after expiration to maintain database
performance. The system ensures tokens are cryptographically secure and
single-use to prevent security vulnerabilities.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_todo_user_id`
  > The todo user associated with this email verification token. {@link
  > todo_app_todo_users.id}
- `code`
  > Cryptographically secure token value used for email verification. This is
  > a unique, random string that is emailed to the user as part of a
  > verification link.
- `expired_at`
  > Expiration timestamp for the email verification token. After this time,
  > the token becomes invalid and the user must request a new verification
  > email.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the email verification token was created.

### `todo_app_configurations`

Application configuration settings that control global behavior and
feature flags for the todo application.

This table stores system-wide configuration values that can be used to
enable or disable features,
set application limits, define operational parameters, and control other
global behaviors.
The configuration uses a key-value structure where each key represents a
specific setting
and the value contains the configuration data in JSON format.

Configurations are identified by unique keys and can be scoped to
specific namespaces
for better organization. The system maintains version history for
configuration changes
and includes temporal fields for audit trails.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `key`
  > Unique key identifying the configuration setting. Must follow naming
  > conventions with lowercase letters, numbers, and underscores only.
  > Examples: 'feature_enable_edit_history', 'limit_max_todos_per_user',
  > 'auth_password_min_length'.
- `namespace`
  > Namespace for organizing configurations. Allows grouping related settings
  > together. Examples: 'auth', 'todo', 'system', 'limits'.
- `value`
  > JSON-formatted configuration value. Can store simple values like strings
  > and numbers, or complex objects and arrays as needed for the specific
  > configuration setting.
- `description`
  > Description of what this configuration setting does and how it should be
  > used. Provides context for system administrators managing configurations.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this configuration entry was created. Used for audit
  > trails and tracking when settings were introduced.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when this configuration entry was last updated. Used for audit
  > trails and tracking when settings were modified.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when this configuration entry was deleted (soft delete). Allows
  > configuration entries to be archived without permanent removal.

### `todo_app_system_settings`

todo_app_system_settings

This table stores key-value pairs of system configuration settings,
including feature flags, operational parameters, and behavioral
configurations that control the overall application functionality. Each
setting is uniquely identified by its name and contains serialized value
data along with descriptive metadata.

Settings are versioned through the todo_app_system_setting_histories
table to maintain an audit trail of all changes.

Use this table to store configuration parameters that affect the entire
application, such as:
- Feature enablement flags
- Performance tuning parameters
- Integration endpoint configurations
- Business rule thresholds
- Operational mode settings

Properties as follows:

- `description`

  > system setting.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the setting was initially created in the system.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the setting was last modified.

### `todo_app_schema_versions`

Tracking table for database schema versions and migration history in the
todo application.

This table maintains a chronological record of all schema changes applied
to the application database. Each entry represents a specific version of
the database schema, allowing for reliable migration management and
rollback capabilities when needed.

The version tracking system ensures that database changes are applied
consistently across different environments (development, staging,
production) and provides audit trails for schema evolution. It supports
automated migration workflows by recording which migrations have been
applied and when.

Each version entry includes metadata about the migration such as version
identifier, description, and timestamps for when the migration was
applied. The system prevents duplicate migrations by enforcing unique
version identifiers.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `version`
  > Primary human-readable identifier for this schema version. Typically
  > follows semantic versioning patterns (e.g., v1.0.0) or migration naming
  > conventions (e.g., 20241201153000_initial_setup).
- `description`
  > Brief description of what changes this schema version introduces.
  > Explains the purpose and impact of the migration for operational
  > understanding.
- `applied_at`
  > Timestamp when this schema version was applied to the database. Used for
  > migration ordering and audit trail purposes.

### `todo_app_todos`

Main todo items created by users in the todo application, containing all
core metadata including title, description, and temporal fields for task
management.

This table represents the primary business entity for the todo
application where users store their task items. Each todo is owned by a
specific user who is authenticated through the todo_app_todo_users
relationship.

Key aspects of this table include:

- Complete ownership tracking through foreign key relationships to user
accounts
- Soft deletion support for the trash system
- Full temporal tracking with created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at
timestamps
- Status tracking with completed boolean field
- Proper indexing strategy for common query patterns

The table is designed to support all user operations including:

- Viewing personal todo lists with pagination
- Creating new todos with optional metadata
- Updating todos with full edit history tracking (handled by History
component)
- Soft deleting todos which moves them to trash (handled by Trash component)
- Filtering and sorting todos by various criteria
- Permanent relationship with user owners for privacy enforcement

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_todo_user_id`: Owner of this todo item. [todo_app_todo_users.id](#todo_app_todo_users).
- `title`
  > Concise summary of what needs to be done. This is the primary identifier
  > users see in their todo lists.
- `description`
  > Detailed explanation or additional context for the todo item. May contain
  > formatting or extended information.
- `start_date`
  > When the user plans to start working on this todo. Used for sorting and
  > filtering todos by start date.
- `due_date`
  > Deadline by which this todo should be completed. Critical for sorting,
  > filtering, and priority management.
- `completed`
  > Whether this todo has been marked as complete by the user. This is the
  > primary status indicator for filtering.
- `created_at`
  > When this todo was originally created by the user. Used for chronological
  > sorting and filtering.
- `updated_at`
  > When this todo was last modified by the user. Used for sorting by recent
  > activity.
- `deleted_at`
  > When this todo was moved to trash (soft delete). Null means active todo,
  > non-null means in trash.

### `todo_app_todo_edit_histories`

Records all edit history entries for todos, capturing detailed
information about every change made to a todo including which fields were
modified and when.

Each history entry represents a single edit event on a todo item and
captures the changes to specific fields (title, description, start date,
due date). This table provides a complete audit trail of all
modifications made to todos over time, which is essential for tracking
changes, recovering previous versions, and understanding how todos
evolve.

History entries are immutable once created and are associated with both
the todo being modified and the user session that performed the edit. The
system only creates entries when actual changes occur - if a user submits
an edit request without making any actual changes to field values, no
history entry is created.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_todo_id`: Reference to the todo item that was edited. [todo_app_todos.id](#todo_app_todos)

  > in this edit.
- `description`

  > was changed in this edit.
- `start_date`
  > The updated start date of the todo item. Only present if the start date
  > was changed in this edit.
- `due_date`
  > The updated due date of the todo item. Only present if the due date was

### `todo_app_trash_entries`

Records all soft-deleted todos, preserving complete todo data and
metadata at the time of deletion for potential restoration or permanent
removal.

This table captures all information about todos when they are moved to
the trash. It maintains the exact state of the todo at deletion time,
including all fields like title, description, dates, and completion
status. This enables full restoration of deleted todos while keeping them
separate from active todos.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to a user who created the original todo
- Maintains reference to original todo data for restoration
- Contains all metadata needed to reconstruct the original todo if restored

This table supports the trash system functionality by:
1. Storing complete todo data when soft deleted
2. Providing data for trash listing views
3. Enabling full restoration of deleted todos
4. Supporting permanent deletion workflows

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_todo_user_id`: The user who created this todo. [todo_app_todo_users.id](#todo_app_todo_users)
- `todo_app_todo_id`: The original todo that was moved to trash. [todo_app_todos.id](#todo_app_todos)
- `title`
  > The title of the todo at the time it was moved to trash. Preserves the
  > original title for potential restoration.
- `description`
  > The description of the todo at the time it was moved to trash. Preserves
  > the original description for potential restoration.
- `start_at`
  > The start date of the todo at the time it was moved to trash. Preserves
  > the original start date for potential restoration.
- `end_at`
  > The due date of the todo at the time it was moved to trash. Preserves the
  > original due date for potential restoration.
- `completed_at`
  > Whether the todo was marked complete at the time it was moved to trash.
  > Preserves the original completion status for potential restoration.
- `created_at`
  > When the todo was originally created, preserved from the original todo
  > for accurate historical tracking.
- `updated_at`
  > When the todo was last updated before being moved to trash, preserved
  > from the original todo for accurate historical tracking.
- `deleted_at`
  > When the todo was moved to trash. This timestamp enables sorting of trash
  > entries by deletion time and supports time-based trash management
  > operations.

### `todo_app_permanent_deletion_records`

Records of todos that have been permanently deleted from the trash system.

This table tracks all todos that have been permanently removed from the
system by users. When a user chooses to permanently delete a todo from
their trash, a record is created in this table containing a reference to
the original todo and the timestamp of deletion. This provides an audit
trail of all permanent deletions for compliance and recovery purposes.

The table is append-only with no updates or deletions allowed after
creation. This ensures a complete and immutable history of all permanent
deletions.

Key relationships:
- References the original todo through the todo_app_todos.id foreign key
- Provides a complete log of user-initiated permanent deletions

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_todo_id`
  > Reference to the original todo that was permanently deleted. {@link
  > todo_app_todos.id}
- `deleted_at`: The timestamp when the todo was permanently deleted by the user.
- `created_at`: The timestamp when this permanent deletion record was created.
- `updated_at`: The timestamp of the last update to this record.

instruction:
# Multi-User Todo Application API Design

## User Account

- Users sign up with email and password
- Users log in with email and password
- Users can change their password
- Users can delete their account (all their todos, including those in trash, are permanently deleted)

## User Profile

- Each user has a profile with: display name
- Users can edit their display name
- Users cannot view other users' profiles (this is a private todo app)

## Creating Todos

- Users can create a todo with:
  - Title (required)
  - Description (optional, can be left empty)
  - Start date (optional, can be left empty)
  - Due date (optional, can be left empty)
- Newly created todos are incomplete by default

## Viewing Todos

- Users can view a list of their own todos
- The list is paginated
- Each todo in the list shows: title, completion status, start date (if set), due date (if set), and creation date
- Users can view a single todo to see all its details including full description

## Completing Todos

- Users can mark a todo as complete
- Users can mark a todo as incomplete
- This is a simple toggle between two states

## Editing Todos

- Users can edit their todo's title, description, start date, and due date
- Every edit is recorded in the todo's history

## Edit History

- Each todo has an edit history
- Every time a todo is edited, a history entry is created
- Each history entry records:
  - When the edit was made
  - What the title was changed to (if changed)
  - What the description was changed to (if changed)
  - What the start date was changed to (if changed)
  - What the due date was changed to (if changed)
- Users can view the full edit history of any of their todos
- History entries are sorted from most recent to oldest

## Deleting Todos

- Users can delete their own todos
- Deleted todos are not permanently removed (soft delete)
- Deleted todos no longer appear in the normal todo list

## Trash

- Users can view a list of their deleted todos (trash)
- The trash list is paginated
- Users can restore a deleted todo from the trash (it returns to the normal todo list)
- Users can permanently delete a todo from the trash
- Permanently deleting a todo also deletes its edit history

## Filtering Todos

- Users can filter their todo list by completion status:
  - All todos
  - Only complete todos
  - Only incomplete todos

## Sorting Todos

- Users can sort their todo list by:
  - Creation date (newest first or oldest first)
  - Start date (earliest first or latest first)
  - Due date (earliest first or latest first)
- Todos without a start date appear at the end when sorting by start date
- Todos without a due date appear at the end when sorting by due date

## Privacy

- Each user's todos are completely private
- Users can only see their own todos
- There is no way to view, access, or share another user's todos

operations.description:
Register a new user account in the todo application.

This endpoint creates a new user profile with the provided email address and password. The email address must be unique across all users in the system. The password will be validated against the system's password complexity requirements before being securely hashed and stored.

The system SHALL collect the email address and password during registration. The email address SHALL be validated for proper format and uniqueness. The password SHALL be validated for complexity requirements before being securely hashed.

Upon successful validation and account creation, the system SHALL return initial authentication tokens to the client, enabling immediate access to the todo management features. The new user account SHALL be created with default settings and an active status.
operations.name: join

requestBody.description: User registration information including email and password.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and user information for the newly registered user.

operations.specification: Implement user registration by validating email uniqueness and password complexity, then create new user record with hashed password. Generate initial JWT tokens for immediate API access. Return tokens along with basic user profile information.

operations.description:
Authenticate a user and establish a session with authentication tokens.

This endpoint validates a user's email and password combination against the stored credentials. Upon successful authentication, the system generates new access and refresh tokens for API access.

The system SHALL validate the email and password combination against stored records. A successful authentication SHALL result in generation of new access and refresh tokens. The system SHALL return these tokens to the client for subsequent API requests.

Failed authentication attempts SHALL be logged for security monitoring. Repeated failed attempts MAY trigger additional security measures such as temporary account lockout or CAPTCHA requirements.

requestBody.description: User credentials for authentication including email and password.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens for the authenticated user.

operations.specification: Validate user credentials against stored hashed password. Generate new JWT access and refresh tokens upon successful authentication. Return tokens to client for API access. Log authentication events for security monitoring.

operations.description:
Refresh authentication tokens using a valid refresh token.

This endpoint accepts a valid refresh token and generates new access and refresh tokens for continued API access. This allows users to maintain their session without needing to re-authenticate with their email and password.

The system SHALL validate the provided refresh token against active sessions. Upon successful validation, the system SHALL invalidate the used refresh token and generate new access and refresh tokens. The system SHALL return these new tokens to the client.

Refresh token invalidation helps maintain security by preventing token reuse. Expired or invalid refresh tokens SHALL result in authentication errors, requiring the user to log in again with their credentials.

operations.description:
Verify a user's email address using a verification token. This endpoint is part of the user registration workflow where users must verify their email address to activate their account. The system validates the provided token against stored verification records and marks the user's email as verified upon successful validation.

The operation integrates with the `todo_app_todo_user_email_verifications` table which stores email verification tokens with their expiration timestamps. It ensures tokens are only valid for a limited time period and can only be used once. When a token is successfully verified, the system updates both the verification record (marking it as used) and the associated user's email_verified status.

Security considerations include rate limiting verification attempts to prevent abuse, validating token integrity, and ensuring tokens can't be reused after successful verification. The system also handles expired tokens appropriately by providing clear error messaging.

This endpoint is typically accessed after a user receives a verification email containing a unique token. It's a critical security step in the authentication flow to confirm email ownership.
operations.name: verifyEmail

requestBody.description: Email verification token to validate

responseBody.description: Successful email verification confirmation

operations.specification:
Validate email verification token against `todo_app_todo_user_email_verifications` table records:
1. Extract token from request body
2. Query database for token record with matching hash
3. Verify token hasn't expired (compare current time with expires_at)
4. Verify token hasn't been used already (check used_at is null)
5. If valid, mark token as used by setting used_at to current timestamp
6. Update associated user's email_verified status to true
7. Return success response with verification timestamp
8. Handle invalid, expired, or already used tokens with appropriate error responses
9. Implement rate limiting on verification attempts
10. Log verification events for security monitoring

operations.description:
Terminate the current user session and log out of the application.

This endpoint handles user logout by invalidating the authentication session associated with the currently authenticated user. The operation requires a valid authentication token in the request headers to identify which session to terminate.

The logout process involves:
1. Validating the provided authentication token
2. Locating the corresponding session record in the user sessions table
3. Removing or invalidating the session record
4. Returning a success response without exposing session details

Security considerations:
- Only authenticated users can access this endpoint
- The operation must validate the token before processing
- Session termination should be immediate and irreversible
- No sensitive session data should be returned in the response

This endpoint interacts with the user sessions database table to ensure proper cleanup of user sessions and maintain application security.
operations.name: logout
operations.specification: Validate the incoming JWT token from request headers and locate the corresponding session record in todo_app_todo_user_sessions table. Delete or invalidate the session record to terminate the user's authentication state. Return an empty successful response with 204 status code to indicate successful logout without exposing any sensitive session information. Handle invalid or expired tokens gracefully without revealing system information.

operations.description:
Update a todo user's profile information including display name.

This operation allows authenticated users to modify their profile information, specifically their display name. The operation operates on the todo_app_todo_users table which stores user profile data including display names. The user is identified by the todoUserId path parameter which corresponds to the user's unique identifier in the system.

Security considerations: Only the authenticated user can update their own profile. The system must verify that the authenticated user matches the todoUserId in the path to prevent unauthorized profile modifications. The operation implements proper input validation to ensure the display name meets system requirements.

The display name is the only user-editable field in the profile as per requirements. Other profile information such as email is managed through separate account management flows. The updated profile information will be reflected immediately in the user's profile and associated todo items.

This operation integrates with the todo_app_todo_users table schema which defines the structure for user profile data. The operation respects the privacy model where users cannot view other users' profiles, ensuring that profile updates are only visible to the user themselves.

Validate that the authenticated user has permission to update this profile (user ID match). Implement input validation for the display_name field according to system requirements. Return the updated user profile object with all relevant fields. Handle cases where the user does not exist by returning appropriate error responses.

operations.description:
Permanently delete a user account and all associated data. This operation completely removes the user from the system along with all their todos. The deletion is irreversible and permanently destroys all user data.

When a user account is deleted, the database automatically performs cascade deletion that removes:
1. All todos created by the user (through foreign key constraints)
2. All edit history entries for the user's todos
3. All trash entries for the user's deleted todos
4. All permanently deleted records for the user

This operation requires the user to be authenticated and authorized to delete their own account. The deletion process is atomic - either all related data is removed successfully or the operation fails and no data is deleted.

Security considerations:
- Only the account owner can perform this operation
- All JWT sessions for the user will be invalidated
- This action cannot be undone
- Rate limiting may apply to prevent abuse
operations.name: erase

operations.specification:
Performs a complete cascade deletion of the user account and all related data. The operation first validates that the authenticated user has permission to delete the specified account (must be the account owner). Then it begins a database transaction that deletes:
1. All todo_app_todo_edit_histories records associated with user's todos
2. All todo_app_trash_entries records for user's todos
3. All todo_app_todos records owned by the user
4. The todo_app_todo_users record itself

The transaction ensures atomicity - if any part fails, the entire operation is rolled back. After successful deletion, all JWT sessions for the user are invalidated and any cached data related to the user is cleared. Rate limiting is applied to prevent abuse of this destructive operation.

operations.description:
Create a new todo item for the authenticated user. This endpoint allows users to create new todo entries in their personal todo list. Each todo must have a title, but description, start date, and due date are optional fields. When created, todos are automatically set to incomplete status by default.

The created todo will be private to the user and will appear in their todo list. Users can later edit, complete, or delete these todos according to the application's features. Every created todo will also begin tracking edit history for any future modifications.

This operation requires authentication and will automatically associate the created todo with the authenticated user's account. All temporal fields should be provided in ISO 8601 format if specified.

Set completion_status to false by default. Validate that the title is provided and not empty. Store all temporal fields in UTC format. Return the complete todo object with its generated ID.

operations.description:
Update an existing todo item with new information. This operation allows authenticated users to modify their own todo items by providing updated values for title, description, start date, and due date. The system automatically records this edit in the todo's history, creating a new entry that captures what fields were changed and when. The updated todo information is then returned in the response.

When updating a todo, users can modify any combination of the supported fields. If a field is not provided in the request, its current value will be preserved. If a field is explicitly set to null, it will clear the existing value (for optional fields like description, start date, and due date). The system validates that the authenticated user is the owner of the todo before applying any changes.

The edit history functionality is automatically managed by the system and tracks all changes to todos. Each history entry contains the timestamp of the edit and the new values for any fields that were modified. This provides users with a complete audit trail of how their todo has evolved over time.

After a successful update, the todo will reflect the new values and the edit history will include a new entry documenting this change. The todo's creation date remains unchanged, but the last modified timestamp will be updated to reflect this edit.
operations.name: update

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target todo item (UUID format)
parameters.name: todoId

responseBody.description: The updated todo item with current values

operations.specification:
Implement a PUT operation to update an existing todo item. The implementation must:
1. Validate that the authenticated user is the owner of the specified todo
2. Retrieve the current todo from the database
3. Apply updates from the request body to the todo
4. Create a new entry in the todo edit history table documenting the changes
5. Update the todo in the database with new values
6. Return the updated todo in the response

For the edit history creation:
- Compare the current todo values with the updated values
- Record which fields were changed and their new values
- Store the edit timestamp and user information
- Link the history entry to the todo

Security considerations:
- Verify todo ownership using the authenticated user's ID
- Validate that the todoId parameter is a valid UUID
- Ensure all updated fields comply with validation rules
- Check that the user has permission to modify todos

Error handling:
- Return 404 if the todoId does not exist
- Return 403 if the user is not the owner of the todo
- Return 400 for validation errors in the request body
- Return 500 for database or server errors

Database operations:
- Query the todo_app_todos table for the existing record
- Update the record with new values
- Insert a new record into todo_app_todo_edit_histories table
- Both operations should be in a transaction to ensure consistency

prerequisites.description: A todo item must exist before it can be updated

operations.description:
Permanently delete a todo item from the system.

This operation performs a hard delete on a specific todo item identified by its unique ID. The operation permanently removes all traces of the todo from the system including the main todo record from the `todo_app_todos` table.

This operation is irreversible and should be used with caution. The authenticated user must be the owner of the todo being deleted.

When successful, this operation returns the deleted todo entity with all its fields as they existed at the time of deletion, including any sensitive information that was part of the todo. The returned entity can be used for confirmation purposes or further processing if needed.

Security considerations:
- Only the owner of the todo can perform this operation
- Proper authentication and authorization checks must be in place
- Rate limiting should be applied to prevent abuse
- Audit logging should record this destructive action

Business rules:
- If the todo doesn't exist, a 404 error should be returned
- If the authenticated user doesn't own the todo, a 403 error should be returned

Related operations:
- GET /todos/{todoId} for retrieving todo details
- PUT /todos/{todoId} for updating todo details
operations.name: erase

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target todo item to be permanently deleted
parameters.name: todoId

responseBody.description: The deleted todo entity with all its fields as they existed at time of deletion

operations.specification:
Implement the permanent deletion of a todo item and its related records:

1. Authorization check: Verify the authenticated user owns the todo
2. Database transaction: Delete todo and all related records atomically
   - Delete all records from `todo_app_todo_edit_histories` where `todo_id` matches
   - Delete any records from `todo_app_trash_entries` where `todo_id` matches
   - Delete the main record from `todo_app_todos`
3. Return the deleted todo entity with all its fields
4. Log the deletion event for audit purposes

Implementation considerations:
- Use database transaction to ensure atomicity
- Validate todo ownership before deletion
- Handle cases where the todo doesn't exist
- Properly handle database errors and rollbacks
- Consider implementing soft delete with a grace period in production environments
- Implement proper error handling with appropriate HTTP status codes

prerequisites.description: Todo must exist before it can be permanently deleted

operations.description:
Create a new edit history entry for a specific todo item.

This operation records a new entry in the todo edit history when a todo item is modified. The edit history captures detailed information about what fields were changed during the edit, including title, description, start date, and due date. Each history entry is timestamped and associated with the specific todo item through its ID.

The operation requires the todoId path parameter to identify which todo the edit history entry belongs to. The request body should contain the details of what was changed in the todo, allowing the system to maintain a comprehensive audit trail of all modifications. This supports the requirement that every edit to a todo is recorded in the todo's history.

Security considerations: Only the owner of the todo can create edit history entries for their todos. The system automatically associates the history entry with the authenticated user based on their session token.

The history entry should capture the changes made to the todo including title, description, start date, and due date if they were modified. Automatically associate the history entry with the authenticated user. Validate that the todo exists and belongs to the authenticated user before creating the history entry. Generate a new UUID for the history entry and timestamp it with the current time.

operations.description:
Permanently delete a todo entry from the trash system.

This operation completely removes a todo entry and all its associated data from the system permanently. When a user deletes a todo from their trash, this endpoint is called to perform the final permanent deletion. The operation removes:

1. The todo entry itself from the trash system
2. All edit history records associated with this todo
3. Any related system tracking records

This is a hard delete operation that cannot be undone. After this operation completes, the todo and all its associated data are completely removed from the database with no possibility of recovery.

Security considerations:
- Only the owner of the todo can perform this operation
- The system validates that the trash entry belongs to the requesting user
- Appropriate rate limiting is applied to prevent abuse
- All related data is cleaned up in a transactional manner to ensure consistency

This endpoint should only be called after explicit user confirmation, as the deletion is irreversible. The related endpoint GET /trash/entries can be used to view items in the trash before permanent deletion.
operations.name: erase

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the trash entry to permanently delete
parameters.name: trashEntryId

operations.specification:
Performs a hard delete operation on a trash entry and all associated data.

1. Validate that the trash entry exists and belongs to the requesting user
2. Begin database transaction
3. Delete all related todo_app_todo_edit_histories records for this todo
4. Delete the todo_app_trash_entries record
5. Commit transaction if all operations succeed
6. Return success response (204 No Content)

The operation uses the Prisma transaction API to ensure all related data is removed consistently. Error handling includes:
- 404 Not Found if trash entry doesn't exist
- 403 Forbidden if user doesn't own the trash entry
- 500 Internal Server Error for database transaction failures

Performance considerations:
- Uses database-level cascading deletes where appropriate
- Implements proper indexing on foreign key relationships
- Logs deletion events for audit purposes

operations.description:
Restore a deleted todo from the trash system back to the user's normal todo list.

This operation moves a todo item from the trash back to the active todo list by clearing its deleted flag, making it visible in normal todo list views. When a todo is restored, all its original properties (title, description, dates, completion status) are preserved, and its complete edit history remains intact. The todo's creation timestamp and all modification history are maintained throughout the restore process.

The system verifies that the trash entry belongs to the authenticated user before performing the restore operation. If the trash entry does not exist or belongs to another user, the operation will fail with an appropriate error response.

After successful restoration, the todo will appear in the user's normal todo list views and will no longer be present in trash listings. The todo's edit history continues to track all changes made before and after the restoration.

operations.specification: Verify the trash entry belongs to the authenticated user by checking the user_id foreign key relationship. Update the todo's deleted status to false (or clear the deleted flag) and set the restored_at timestamp. Remove the trash entry record from the todo_app_trash_entries table. Return the complete todo object with all its properties and relationships intact. Handle the case where the trash entry doesn't exist or doesn't belong to the user by returning an appropriate error response.

operations.description:
Create a record of a permanently deleted todo item in the trash system.

This operation adds a record to the permanent deletion records table when a user permanently deletes a todo from the trash. The record captures metadata about the deletion including when it occurred and which todo was permanently removed. This provides an audit trail of all permanent deletions in the system.

This operation integrates with the trash system as defined in the database schema, specifically the 'todo_app_permanent_deletion_records' table. The permanent deletion record contains information about the deleted todo and maintains a history of all todos that have been permanently removed from the system.

Related operations include viewing trash entries (GET /trash), restoring from trash (PUT /trash/{id}/restore), and listing permanent deletion records (GET /trash/permanent-deletion-records).
operations.name: create

Return the created record with all relevant metadata.

operations.description:

The configuration settings are stored in the todo_app_configurations table which contains key-value pairs for different configuration options.

The created configuration will be used to control global application behavior such as feature flags, system limits, and other configurable parameters that affect all users of the application. Each configuration entry consists of a unique key, a value, and an optional description.

Only authorized todo users should have access to this operation as it affects the entire application's behavior. Regular users without configuration management permissions should not be able to access this endpoint.

operations.description:
Update a specific configuration in the todo application.

This operation allows authenticated users to modify their application configuration settings. The configuration is identified by its unique ID and can include various user preferences and application settings. The operation performs a full replacement of the configuration data with the provided values.

Security considerations: Only the owner of the configuration can modify it. The system validates that the authenticated user has permission to access and modify the specified configuration. Rate limiting may be applied to prevent excessive updates.

When updating configurations, the system ensures data integrity by validating all provided values against their expected types and formats. The configuration data is stored in the todo_app_configurations table, which maintains a history of changes for auditing purposes.

Error handling: The operation returns appropriate HTTP status codes for various error conditions including 404 if the configuration doesn't exist, 403 if the user lacks permission, and 400 for validation errors.

The operation accepts a set of configuration values that define application behavior.
If a setting with the same key already exists, it will be updated with the new value.
If it doesn't exist, a new setting will be created.

This is a system-level configuration endpoint that should only be accessible to administrators.
Regular users should not have access to this functionality as it affects the entire application.

The settings are stored in the todo_app_system_settings table which contains key-value pairs
where each key represents a specific configuration option and the value represents its setting.

Related operations include retrieving current system settings (GET /system/settings) and
resetting settings to default values (DELETE /system/settings/{settingKey}).

Create a new system setting or update an existing one with the same key.

- Only administrators can access this endpoint

Before deletion, the system validates:

Upon successful deletion, the system confirms the operation completion. The operation is idempotent - attempting to delete a non-existent setting will return a success response (following the principle that the desired state is achieved).

operations.description:
Create a new schema version entry to track database schema changes and migrations.

This administrative operation allows system administrators to record new schema versions in the todo application's schema tracking system. Each schema version entry contains metadata about when the schema change occurred, who made the change (if applicable), and descriptive information about the changes made.

The operation creates a new record in the todo_app_schema_versions table, which serves as the authoritative log of all database schema modifications. This tracking mechanism is essential for:

1. Database migration history - Maintaining a chronological record of all schema changes
2. Rollback planning - Enabling administrators to understand what changes can be reversed
3. System auditing - Providing visibility into database evolution over time
4. Troubleshooting - Helping identify when specific schema changes were implemented

When creating a new schema version entry, the system automatically timestamps the record creation. All schema version entries are immutable once created to maintain audit integrity.

Related operations that work with schema versions include:
- GET /schema/versions - List all schema versions chronologically
- GET /schema/versions/{id} - Retrieve specific schema version details

This write operation should only be performed by authorized system administrators during legitimate database migration processes.

Only administrative users with appropriate permissions should be allowed to modify schema version records, as these are system-level metadata items that track database migration history.

This endpoint directly operates on the todo_app_schema_versions database table and maintains all the same constraints and validation rules as defined in the schema. The id field serves as the unique identifier and cannot be modified through this operation - only the descriptive metadata can be updated.

Handle cases where the version ID does not exist by returning an appropriate error response. Ensure all database constraints are maintained during the update process.

The operation requires a valid version identifier (UUID format) to locate and permanently remove the specific schema version record. This is a hard delete operation that completely removes all tracking information associated with that version from the system.

Security Considerations:

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of the authenticated user's todos with basic information including title, completion status, dates, and creation timestamp.

This endpoint returns a paginated collection of todos belonging to the authenticated user. Each todo in the response includes essential information for list display: title, completion status, start date (if set), due date (if set), and creation date. The todos are filtered to show only those belonging to the current user, implementing the strict privacy requirement that users can only access their own todos.

The response uses pagination to handle potentially large numbers of todos efficiently. Users can page through their todo list with configurable page sizes. The todos in the list view contain only summary information - for complete todo details including full description and edit history, users should retrieve individual todos via the detail endpoint.

Related operations include creating new todos (POST /todos), viewing individual todo details (GET /todos/{todoId}), and managing todo states (PUT /todos/{todoId}/complete, PUT /todos/{todoId}/incomplete). For managing deleted todos, users can access the trash system (PATCH /trash).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of user's todos with summary information

Order by created_at descending by default. Implement pagination with configurable page size (default 20, max 100). Apply user isolation filter to ensure users only see their own todos. Include totalCount in pagination metadata.

operations.description:
Search and filter todos with pagination, sorting, and completion status filtering.

This operation allows authenticated users to search their personal todo list with advanced filtering capabilities. Users can filter todos by completion status and sort results by creation date, start date, or due date. The operation implements pagination to handle large todo lists efficiently.

The search functionality supports:
- Filtering by completion status (all, complete, incomplete)
- Sorting by creation date (newest/oldest first)
- Sorting by start date (earliest/latest first)
- Sorting by due date (earliest/latest first)
- Pagination with configurable page size

When sorting by start date or due date, todos without those dates will appear at the end of the list as specified in the requirements. The response includes a paginated list of todo summaries with essential information for quick overview.

Security considerations: Only authenticated users can access their own todos. The system enforces strict data isolation to prevent users from accessing other users' todo data. All filtering and sorting operations are performed server-side to ensure data privacy.

Related operations: Users can view detailed todo information with GET /todos/{todoId}, create new todos with POST /todos, and manage todo completion status with PUT /todos/{todoId}/complete.
operations.name: index

responseBody.description: Paginated list of todo summaries matching search criteria

Filter results to only include todos belonging to the authenticated user. Sort by creation date by default (newest first), with options to sort by start date or due date. When sorting by start or due date, place todos without those dates at the end of the list. Return IPageITodoAppTodo.ISummary response with pagination metadata.
